questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The quality of education at the host university and the possibility to participate in subjects which were not available to me at UCPH.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of information provided through University of Melbourne's website but it could also be a bit overwhelming.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Melbourne provided a lot of information through emails and during the orientation days which was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It took some time (3 weeks) to find housing on my own but it was possible and I got a lot more value for money by doing so. I found housing though the Facebook group Fairy Floss by making a housing search post. I had a lot of people reach out to me - some legit some not. Still, it worked out very well in the end by doing so. It takes a bit of patience and can be quite stressful but it usually works out very well in the end.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice being able to explore other parts of Melbourne other than just around campus. It gives you the opportunity to potentially meet locals.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: From what I heard housing through the university or other agencies can be very expensive and you won't necessarily get a lot of value for your money. This being said it is a lot easier and convenient if you want to plan it prior to your arrival.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A guide was available but I found the website quite confusing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Yes you can contact Stop1. They were very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to get help registering for one of my classes as it was an undergrad subject and I was enrolled as a postgraduate. It just meant I had to fill out an application to get stop1 to proceed with the registration.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It takes a bit of time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did three MA and one BA level which gave me the opportunity to diversify the study load.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UniMelb predominately had lectures and not a lot of tutorials within the subjects I followed. This meant they studying could feel a bit isolating as I was not able to have a study group.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Australian Surfing (BA)
Health Program Evaluation 1 (MA)
Public Health in Practice (MA)
Gender and Health (MA)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Gender and Health (MA) was really interesting and gave me a lot of new perspectives that I find very useful for my future work.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing is paid weekly so some months will be more expensive than others depending on the amount of weeks. Eating out is less expensive than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of opportunities which were all presented during orientation week. It can feel quite overwhelming though.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of clubs and free events you were able to sign up for.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try to join a club or some of the trips you will be able to meet people through that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to a footy game - you cant miss that. Tasmania is not too far away and is worth a visit. Grampians and Phillips Island are stunning too.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I felt that only 1/3 of the students at UniMelb actually attended classes and most participated online. This made it difficult to meet people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The laid backness. People are usually easy to talk to but it may be difficult to actually become close.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Finding off campus housing on your own takes time and can be nerve wrecking, but it will usually work out. 
You may feel very isolated at times but remember so does everyone so open up about it.
Remember to go explore while you are there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be tough at times but it is also very rewarding.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Personally meeting old and new friends. Academically getting new perspectives.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling isolated and alone at uni due to the lack of a study group.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
